clues: Pillow basalts and other exposed rocks allow the ocean floor’s geological history to be examined on land.
The island is an exposed crest of a largely submarine ridge.
Uplift near a plate boundary has brought deep oceanic rocks, including mantle material, above sea level.
A long Australian scientific presence accompanies large concentrations of penguins, seals and seabirds.
Find the narrow Australian subantarctic island south-east of Tasmania, roughly halfway towards Antarctica.
targetLabel: Macquarie Island — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: The island provides geological evidence of an oceanic ridge and deep rocks raised above sea level. The Australian Antarctic Division also describes its scientific station and abundant breeding wildlife. The official island-property reference point is used; it is not necessarily the station or a wildlife colony.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
